controls.name: dotdot_literal_check
controls.description: Rejects any individual part containing a literal '..' segment (plus any absolute component), but never normalizes-and-compares against base at all. This over-rejects a legitimate '..' that still resolves within base (e.g. "reports/../public"), because it looks only at the raw, pre-join part text rather than the resolved path. A plausible 'forgot the allowed edge case' fix: the author reasoned '..' is always dangerous and blocked it outright instead of checking containment.

controls.name: normalized_dotdot_token_check
controls.description: Checks for absolute components, then normalizes the joined path and rejects it only if a literal '..' token survives normalization. Since posixpath.normpath collapses every resolvable '..' for an absolute base, this check almost never fires: e.g. base "/srv/data", part "../etc/passwd" normalizes straight to "/srv/etc/passwd" with no '..' left, so the escape sails through silently. A realistic 'missing validation' bug: the author normalizes but never actually compares the result against base.

controls.name: wrong_exception_type
controls.description: Containment logic is otherwise correct (mirrors the reference's normalize-then-prefix-check), but raises PermissionError instead of the required ValueError on an escape. A plausible slip: the author copied an access-control pattern from elsewhere in the codebase and kept its exception type instead of switching to ValueError as the task spec requires. Every hidden test that does pytest.raises(ValueError) on an escaping input fails because PermissionError propagates uncaught.

controls.name: prefix_startswith_no_separator
controls.description: Reintroduces the historical prefix-collision bug this task's reference used to have: containment is enforced via a naive norm_joined.startswith(norm_base) with NO trailing-separator check. A sibling directory that merely shares a name prefix (e.g. "/srv/data-other") is wrongly treated as being under base "/srv/data", because the string "/srv/data-other/file.txt" literally starts with the string "/srv/data". This is exactly the task-specific security near-miss a partial or naive fix of safe_join is likely to reproduce.

controls.name: segment_stack_resolution
controls.description: Structurally different but behaviorally equivalent correct solution: instead of normalizing the whole joined string with posixpath.normpath and then doing a str.startswith prefix compare, this walks base's segments plus every part's segments onto one explicit list-stack (the same left-to-right resolution normpath performs internally), allowing a transient climb above base that comes back down before the walk ends, and only checks the FINAL resolved position against base -- via list-prefix comparison, not string prefix -- so it also can never be fooled by a same-prefix sibling like '/srv/data-other'.

findings.summary: A `_pytest/` package directory is not flagged as a protected-path violation, though grading runs pytest with the cleanroom at sys.path[0].
findings.detail: Injecting 'safepath/_pytest/__init__.py' was NOT flagged as touching a protected path. ALWAYS_PROTECTED_BASENAMES matches basenames, not directory names, so a submission-created `_pytest/` package shadowing the real `_pytest` internals package is currently only stopped by this task's editable_paths allow-list (when configured), not by a structural guarantee. See docs/agents/ORACLE.md for why this is reported rather than silently fixed here.
